title: Price alerts service
context: Design a service that lets users set price alerts ("notify me when TSLA goes above 300"). Scale: 5 million users, 20 million active alerts across 15,000 instruments. The market data feed sends about 50,000 price ticks per second. A push notification should arrive within 2 seconds of the price crossing, and each alert fires once. Describe the components, data model, how alerts are matched against ticks, and how you keep it reliable.
answer: Store alerts durably in a database, and keep an in-memory index per instrument: two sorted structures (above and below thresholds) so each tick is a range query for crossed alerts instead of a scan. Consume ticks from Kafka partitioned by instrument, so each matcher instance owns a set of instruments and rebuilds its index from the database on startup. When an alert crosses, mark it triggered with a conditional update (only if still active) so it fires exactly once even after a restart or rebalance, then publish a notification event. A separate notification service sends pushes with retries, a dead-letter queue and per-user rate limits. Handle hot instruments by splitting their alerts across more partitions, and watch end-to-end latency from tick to push.

points.title: Index alerts by instrument and threshold
points.why: Scanning 20M alerts per tick is impossible; sorted thresholds per instrument make each tick a range lookup.

points.title: Partition the work by instrument
points.why: Kafka partitions (or consistent hashing) by instrument let matcher instances scale out and keep ordering per instrument.

points.title: Fire each alert exactly once
points.why: Restarts and redelivery can re-match the same alert; an atomic state change prevents duplicate pushes.

points.title: Durable store plus rebuildable index
points.why: Alerts live in a database; in-memory or Redis indexes are rebuilt from it after a crash.

points.title: Separate, reliable notification path
points.why: Pushes go through a queue with retries, a dead-letter queue and per-user limits, so slow push providers don't slow matching.

points.title: Hot instruments and latency monitoring
points.why: A few instruments get most ticks and alerts; split them further and track tick-to-push latency against the 2 s target.
